title: Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
summary: Compartment epidemic models are often linear in coefficients that are physical parameters or products of parameters, so parameter estimation can be reduced to closed-form least squares. The paper introduces physics-informed weak regression (PIWR), which integrates the model in time with cubic-spline quadrature, avoids differentiating noisy data, estimates the initial state jointly, and is wrapped with split conformal prediction using simulated epidemics as the calibration population, plus a residual-adaptive factor (PIWR-RACC). Across eleven DINN benchmarks, PIWR or PIR-FD6 is reported to improve on DINN errors by one to four orders of magnitude where sampling resolves the dynamics, each fit takes about a millisecond, and the 90% simultaneous intervals achieve 87–92% empirical coverage in all 88 tested settings.

target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.split: 100 samples on [0,500] days; ε=0.01 noise level
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01
target.config_for_value: PIWR with cubic-spline quadrature and jointly estimated initial state; SIDR parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294; N=59·10^6; 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days; 1 % multiplicative Gaussian noise
target.est_compute: CPU, <1 s including data simulation; single PIWR fit is about 0.2 ms
target.quote: With 1 % noise the error of PIR-FD2 grows to 1.2–1.5 %, while PIR-FD6 and PIWR reach 0.12–0.49 %.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

claims.quote: PIR-FD6 reduces it to 0.002–0.003 %, and PIWR to 0.0001 %, four orders of magnitude below DINN

requirements.stmt: Formulate the epidemic model in parameter-linear form ẋ = f0(x,t) + A(x,t)θ, with the library A containing no unknown parameters and a map h recovering physical parameters from θ.
requirements.quote: the library A(x, t) ∈Rn×p contains no unknowns

requirements.stmt: For PIWR, use the integrated weak relation x(tj)=x0+Jjθ, with Jj the time integral of the library, instead of differentiating the data.
requirements.quote: The relation is still linear in θ, but it contains the data themselves instead of their derivatives.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate each library entry by a cubic spline with not-a-knot end conditions on the sample grid and integrate the spline exactly to obtain quadrature weights.
requirements.quote: interpolated over t0, . . . , tm−1 by a cubic spline (not-a-knot end conditions), and the spline is integrated exactly from t0 to tj.

requirements.stmt: Estimate the initial state x0 jointly with θ using the augmented system with identity blocks for x0.
requirements.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns, so that the noise of the first sample is not propagated into every equation.

requirements.stmt: Solve the PIWR least-squares problem by a numerically stable orthogonal factorization or SVD-based least squares, not by explicitly forming the normal equations.
requirements.quote: In implementation, we do not form the normal equations (16), whose condition number is the square of that of MD.

requirements.stmt: Column-scale the regression matrix to unit column norm before the solve; scaling is a change of variables and leaves the minimizer unchanged.
requirements.cite: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, equations (11) and implementation after (18)
requirements.quote: the columns are scaled to unit norm before the solve

requirements.stmt: For the synthetic benchmarks, add compartment-wise noise with standard deviation ε times the maximum absolute true compartment value over the time grid.
requirements.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

requirements.stmt: For conformal calibration, draw calibration parameters from a prior box of ±50 % around literature values, capped at 1 for probabilities and [0,c] for parameters whose literature value is zero.
requirements.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

requirements.stmt: Use the maximum normalized error over all parameters as the split-conformal nonconformity score, then form simultaneous intervals with the corresponding quantile.
requirements.quote: To obtain intervals that hold for all k parameters at once, we use the maximum normalized error as the nonconformity score

requirements.stmt: For PIWR-RACC, compute the residual-adaptive factor h = 1 + R/Rbar, with Rbar the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and apply h to scores and intervals.
requirements.quote: with  ̄R the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and use it in the score (20) and the intervals (21).

requirements.stmt: Use 999 calibration problems and α=0.1 for the 90 % simultaneous intervals, with tuning done on separate draws.
requirements.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1.

requirements.stmt: Recover physical parameters through ω=h(θ) and, when uncertainty in ω is reported, propagate the coefficient covariance by the delta method.
requirements.quote: The physical parameters are ˆω = h(ˆθ). Their uncertainty follows from the delta method

requirements.stmt: For the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark, use N=59·10^6, initial state S0=N−1 and I0=1, parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294, and 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days.
requirements.cite: Section 2 worked example and Appendix A.1
requirements.quote: 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days (∆t = 5.05 days) of the solution with (α, β, γ) = (0.191, 0.05, 0.0294)

requirements.stmt: Report errors as percent of the actual parameter value, using the median over estimated parameters of a model when summarizing a model.
requirements.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

requirements.stmt: Generate synthetic benchmark trajectories with LSODA at relative and absolute tolerances of 10^-10.
requirements.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The paper does not give the random seed or specify whether the Table 2 PIWR value 0.124 % is from one noise realization, a median over realizations, or a repeated-fit median.
assumptions.chosen: Use a single fixed-seed realization for the point estimate, then check stability over 1,000 realizations at the literature values.
assumptions.quote: for ε = 1 %, on 1,000 noise realizations at the literature values.

assumptions.gap: The paper says row scaling is selected per model on tuning draws but does not state whether the SIDR PIWR run uses Dn=In or compartment-max scaling.
assumptions.chosen: Use Dn=In for SIDR unless a separate tuning run on 100 draws says otherwise.
assumptions.quote: whether to use it (Dn = In otherwise) is decided per model and estimator on a tuning set (section 5.1).

assumptions.gap: The exact definition of the reported single-parameter % error for α is not given beyond the general metric sentence.
assumptions.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

assumptions.gap: The initial state x0 is estimated jointly but the paper does not state whether positivity or bounds are imposed on x0.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained least squares, as in the augmented linear system.
assumptions.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns

assumptions.gap: The exact ODE solver tolerances for the synthetic SIDR data generation are not stated in the main text.
assumptions.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The printed Δt=5.05 days is rounded; the exact grid construction is not shown.
The population is printed as 59·10^6 in OCR text; the exact integer is not otherwise specified.
The paper does not say whether any smoothing is applied to noisy states before evaluating the library inside the PIWR integrals.
assumptions.chosen: No smoothing; use noisy states directly in the library and integrate by spline.
assumptions.quote: Both PIR and PIWR evaluate the library at the noisy samples.

assumptions.gap: The least-squares rank-deficiency threshold and exact SVD/LAPACK routine are not specified.
assumptions.chosen: numpy.linalg.lstsq with default rcond in float64.

assumptions.gap: The exact joint prior box for α, β, γ in the SIDR calibration is not tabulated parameter by parameter.
assumptions.chosen: Independent uniform [0.5α*,1.5α*], [0.5β*,1.5β*], [0.5γ*,1.5γ*], with no cap binding since all values are below 1.
assumptions.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

assumptions.gap: The random seeds for the 100 row-scaling tuning draws and 200 Rbar tuning draws are not given.
assumptions.chosen: Use separate fixed seeds for row-scaling tuning, Rbar tuning, calibration, and testing.
assumptions.quote: Every estimator is tuned on draws that are not used for calibration or testing: the row scaling on 100 draws,  ̄R on 200 draws.

assumptions.gap: The seed splitting for 999 calibration problems and 2,000 test problems is not specified.
assumptions.chosen: Use fixed seed 0 and disjoint generated pools for calibration and testing.
assumptions.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1. The coverage is measured on 2,000 independent test problems

assumptions.gap: Whether coverage is evaluated for all parameters simultaneously or marginally is not fully explicit in the table rows.
assumptions.chosen: Use simultaneous coverage of all parameters in the model, matching the conformal score.

assumptions.gap: The numerical precision and implementation language for the least-squares solve are not part of the mathematical method but affect exact values.
assumptions.quote: all estimates are dense least-squares solves (numpy.linalg.lstsq) in double precision.

assumptions.gap: Whether the RACC h factor is used for the point estimate or only for interval widths is not explicit in the score formula text.
assumptions.chosen: Apply h only to scores and interval widths; point estimate remains the PIWR least-squares estimate.
assumptions.quote: Scaling the conformal scores and intervals by a factor that increases with this residual widens the intervals for difficult data sets and narrows them for easy ones

assumptions.gap: The paper does not state whether the first and last samples are included in the PIWR linear system beyond saying all samples are used.
assumptions.chosen: Include all m samples, with J0=0 and the measured x0 on the right-hand side.
assumptions.quote: uses all samples, including the end points

assumptions.gap: The paper does not constrain the SIDR parameter estimates to be positive or within a physical range.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained linear least squares for the point estimate.
assumptions.quote: PIR and PIWR search an unbounded parameter space

assumptions.gap: The noise scale uses the maximum true compartment value, but the paper does not state whether that maximum is computed before or after adding noise.
assumptions.chosen: Maximum of the true noise-free trajectory per compartment.
assumptions.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

why: The only linked repository (Shaier/DINN) is the *baseline* the paper benchmarks against, not the paper's own method: it contains 626 files of Jupyter notebooks and CSVs for DINN training, zero Python modules, and no PIWR / PIR-FD / conformal-prediction code at all. The paper's contribution (physics-informed weak regression: integrate the linear-in-parameters SIDR equations in time with cubic-spline quadrature, solve a closed-form least-squares problem with the initial state as a free unknown) exists only as a mathematical description in the text, so it must be reimplemented. The repo is still useful in one narrow way: Diseases/COVID/generate_covid_data.ipynb and sidr.csv pin down the exact SIDR benchmark (N = 59e6, S0 = N-1, I0 = 1, alpha = 0.191, beta = 0.05, gamma = 0.0294, 100 points on [0,500], 1% multiplicative noise), which is the match target for C1, and the data can equally be regenerated from Appendix A.1 alone. The reimplementation is cheap: a 4-state linear ODE system, a cumulative-spline quadrature matrix, and one numpy.linalg.lstsq call.
est_runtime: 5-10 minutes of command time: ~1 min to install numpy/scipy/matplotlib, ~10 s to simulate the SIDR benchmark, milliseconds per PIWR fit, so a few hundred repeated fits plus a noise-level sweep finish in seconds; the remainder is development of the ~200-line weak-form estimator and the clean re-run.
blockers: The linked repository is the DINN baseline (PyTorch 1.8.1, pandas 1.1.5, numpy 1.19.2, Python 3.6) — the paper's own estimator is not in it, so nothing in the repo produces any of the claimed numbers

requirements.txt pins torch/numpy versions that will not install cleanly on this machine's Python 3.12, but that is moot since the DINN baseline is the comparison method and not needed for the match target
No scripts, only notebooks; no CLI entrypoint that emits a target number

The two runs reported for C1 are single noise realizations implicitly (no seed stated), so an exact 0.124% match requires reproducing the same random draw; honest reproduction should report median/mean over realizations and accept a small deviation

approach: Reimplement PIWR for the SIDR benchmark directly from the equations: generate the true trajectory with LSODA at 1e-10 tolerances, and for C1 use the 100-point DINN `sidr.csv` 1% benchmark when available (falling back to a fixed-seed regeneration from Appendix A.1) so the single noise realisation is not invented. For each compartment and each library column, evaluate A(x,t) on the sample grid, interpolate with a not-a-knot cubic spline, integrate the spline exactly to every sample time, and assemble the augmented linear system with x0 as four extra unknowns. Solve the column-normalised system with `numpy.linalg.lstsq` (never forming normal equations), unscale, extract theta=(alpha,beta,gamma), and compute |alpha_hat-0.191|/0.191*100. Add noiseless, stability-over-realizations, and timing checks, then write all numbers to `results/metrics.json`.
steps: Create `config.py` with the exact SIDR parameters, time grid, noise level, LSODA tolerances, spline/quadrature settings, column scaling, lstsq settings, target and tolerance; do not install DINN requirements or run DINN notebooks.
Implement `src/sidr.py`: SIDR RHS with state order [S,I,D,R], LSODA simulation at rtol=atol=1e-10, compartment-wise Gaussian noise per R7, and a flexible CSV loader for the DINN `sidr.csv` benchmark.

Load `Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv` if present; inspect header/columns and confirm there are 100 rows with time plus S,I,D,R. Compare it with a noiseless LSODA trajectory to verify it is the 1% noise file. If it is missing or not the 1% file, use `Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv`; if no candidate CSV exists, regenerate with seed 0.

Implement `src/piwr.py`: for each state c and each library column k, evaluate A_{c,k}(x_noisy(t_i),t_i) on the sample grid, build a not-a-knot CubicSpline, integrate exactly from t_0 to every t_j via the spline antiderivative, and store J[c][j,k].

Build the augmented system M and RHS y: for each state c and time j, set M[row,c]=1 for x0_c and M[row,n_states+k]=J[c][j,k] for theta_k; set y[row]=x_noisy[j,c]. Include all m samples and ensure J[:,0]=0 at j=0.

Column-scale M to unit column norms, solve with `numpy.linalg.lstsq(M_scaled,y,rcond=None)` in float64, unscale coefficients by dividing by the column norms, and extract x0_hat and theta_hat=(alpha_hat,beta_hat,gamma_hat).

Run the noiseless sanity fit on the true trajectory: verify alpha_hat is within about 1e-4% of 0.191 and x0_hat matches the true initial state; if not, debug the SIDR library, spline integration, or state/column mapping before touching the 1% data.
Run the C1 fit on the verified 1% benchmark CSV: compute alpha_hat and `100*abs(alpha_hat-0.191)/0.191`; record whether it lies in [0.1116,0.1364].
Run the stability sweep: regenerate 1000 independent 1% noise realisations with fixed seeds, fit each with PIWR, and store median, mean, IQR and 5–95% range of the alpha percent error.
Run the timing check: repeat the PIWR fit 30 times on the C1 data set and record median CPU milliseconds per fit.

Write `results/metrics.json` with the C1 headline fields (alpha_true, alpha_hat, alpha_rel_error_pct, target_pct, within_tolerance), data source, matrix shape/rank/condition number, x0_hat, beta_hat, gamma_hat, noiseless check, stability summary, timing summary, and the exact config used.

Validate the JSON by re-reading it and printing a summary; verify the headline error is compared against the relative tolerance band and that the noiseless, stability and timing diagnostics are present.
smoke_test: Implement a `--smoke` mode in `reproduce.py` that loads/simulates the SIDR benchmark once, builds M, asserts M.shape==(400,7), asserts J_0==0, checks rank(M_scaled)==7, and runs two fits: (i) noiseless true states, expected alpha error below 1e-4%, and (ii) one noisy 1% realisation, expected alpha error in the 0.05–1% range. This proves the spline quadrature, augmented least squares, scaling, and alpha extraction without the 1000-realisation sweep.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: t has shape (100,), X_noisy has shape (100,4), all finite; time runs from 0 to 500 inclusive with `np.linspace(0,500,100)`.
True trajectory sanity: S decreases from N-1, I starts at 1 and peaks, D and R are nonnegative and nondecreasing; max absolute value per compartment is nonzero so the R7 noise scale is well defined.

Noise sanity on the benchmark CSV: if using `sidr.csv`, compare it with the noiseless trajectory and verify residuals are approximately N(0, (0.01*max|x_c|)^2); if not, select the correct 100-point 1% noise CSV before fitting.
Matrix sanity: M has shape (4*100,4+3)=(400,7); J at t_0 is exactly zero for every column; after unit-column scaling no column has zero norm; rank is 7 and the scaled condition number is reported.

Noiseless baseline: a PIWR fit to the true states recovers alpha to near machine/quadrature accuracy (target <1e-4% relative error) and gives x0 close to [N-1,1,0,0]; failure here means an equation/library/quadrature bug, not a noise issue.
Single noisy fit sanity: alpha_hat is positive and within a few percent of 0.191; the reported C1 error should be near the paper's 0.124%, not orders of magnitude larger.
Timing sanity: 30 repeated fits on the 100-point SIDR problem should be milliseconds or less on CPU; if a fit takes seconds, the implementation is rebuilding splines or solving the wrong problem.
budget_plan: About 10 minutes of command time: 2 min creating `config.py`, `src/sidr.py`, `src/piwr.py`, `src/evaluate.py`, and `reproduce.py`; 2 min on smoke/noiseless validation and fixing any shape or quadrature bug; 3 min on the C1 fit plus the 1000-realisation stability sweep (each fit is sub-millisecond to millisecond, so the sweep is dominated by data generation and Python overhead); 1 min for the 30-repeat timing check; 2 min for writing, re-reading, and validating `results/metrics.json`.

"""Single source of truth for the COVID-19 SIDR PIWR reproduction.

Everything the paper pins down for the C1/C2 match target (parameters, grid,
noise model, solver tolerances, quadrature and least-squares settings) lives
here.  Nothing in this file is a *result*: the true parameters below are the
data-generating constants listed in the paper (Appendix A.1 / section 2).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model: COVID-19 SIDR (paper eq. (5), Appendix A.1)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
POPULATION_N = 59e6                 # known population
STATE_ORDER = ("S", "I", "D", "R")  # n = 4
# x0 = (N-1, 1, 0, 0)
X0_TRUE = (POPULATION_N - 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# true (data generating) physical parameters, eq. (29)
TRUE_PARAMS = {
    "alpha": 0.191,   # transmission rate
    "beta": 0.05,     # recovery rate (term beta*I in dR/dt)
    "gamma": 0.0294,  # death rate      (term gamma*I in dD/dt)
}
PARAM_NAMES = ("alpha", "beta", "gamma")   # theta = (alpha, beta, gamma), p = 3
THETA_TRUE = tuple(TRUE_PARAMS[k] for k in PARAM_NAMES)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sampling grid and noise
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
M_SAMPLES = 100
T_START = 0.0
T_END = 500.0

NOISE_EPS_SMALL = 1e-2   # the C1 setting  (1 % noise)
NOISE_EPS_ZERO = 0.0     # the C2 setting  (noise free)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ODE integration: LSODA at rtol = atol = 1e-10 (Appendix A)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ODE_METHOD = "LSODA"
ODE_RTOL = 1e-10
ODE_ATOL = 1e-10

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Estimator settings
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
SPLINE_BC = "not-a-knot"      # cubic spline end conditions, eq. (13)
joint_initial_state = True    # x0 as n additional unknowns, eq. (14)
LSTSQ_RCOND = None            # SVD based numpy.linalg.lstsq, never normal eqs
COLUMN_SCALE = True           # unit column norm before the solve, eq. (11)

# Row scaling D_n = diag(1/max_i|x_i,c|) is *tuned* by the paper on separate
# draws (section 5.1).  The tuning is done in reproduce.py on `N_TUNING_DRAWS`
# draws and the selected setting is reported in results/metrics.json.
ROW_SCALING_OPTIONS = (False, True)
N_TUNING_DRAWS = 100          # section 5.1: "the row scaling on 100 draws"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Repetition counts for the diagnostics
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
N_NOISE_REALIZATIONS = 1000   # section 5.1: 1,000 noise realizations at lit. values
N_TIMING_REPEATS = 30         # paper: "median of 30 repeated fits of one data set"
SEED_BASE = 0

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
REPO = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "repo")
DINN_SIDR_CSV = os.path.join(REPO, "Diseases", "COVID", "sidr.csv")
RESULTS_DIR = "results"
METRICS_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "metrics.json")

"""COVID-19 SIDR benchmark: generation of the synthetic data.

Paper eq. (5) / Appendix A.1:
    dS/dt = -alpha S I / N
    dI/dt =  alpha S I / N - (beta + gamma) I
    dD/dt =  gamma I
    dR/dt =  beta  I
with x0 = (N-1, 1, 0, 0), (alpha, beta, gamma) = (0.191, 0.05, 0.0294),
N = 59e6, and 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp


def sidr_rhs(t, x, alpha, beta, gamma, N):
    S, I, D, R = x
    infection = alpha * S * I / N
    return [
        -infection,
        infection - (beta + gamma) * I,
        gamma * I,
        beta * I,
    ]


def time_grid(m=100, t0=0.0, T=500.0):
    """Equally spaced sample grid, endpoints included."""
    return np.linspace(t0, T, m)


def simulate(t, params=(0.191, 0.05, 0.0294), x0=None, N=59e6,
             rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10, method="LSODA"):
    """Integrate the SIDR IVP and return the states at the sample times.

    Returns an array of shape (m, 4) with state order (S, I, D, R).
    """
    alpha, beta, gamma = params
    if x0 is None:
        x0 = (N - 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    sol = solve_ivp(
        sidr_rhs,
        (float(t[0]), float(t[-1])),
        np.asarray(x0, dtype=float),
        method=method,
        t_eval=t,
        args=(alpha, beta, gamma, N),
        rtol=rtol,
        atol=atol,
    )
    if not sol.success:  # pragma: no cover
        raise RuntimeError(f"ODE integration failed: {sol.message}")
    return sol.y.T.copy()


def add_noise(x_true, eps, rng):
    """Compartment-wise noise, paper section 5.1 / requirement R7:

        x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + eps * max_t |x_c(t)| * xi_i,  xi_i ~ N(0,1)

    independent per compartment and per sample.
    """
    x_true = np.asarray(x_true, dtype=float)
    if eps == 0.0:
        return x_true.copy()
    scale = eps * np.max(np.abs(x_true), axis=0)          # (n,)
    return x_true + scale[None, :] * rng.standard_normal(x_true.shape)


def load_dinn_csv(path):
    """Load the DINN ``sidr.csv`` benchmark (rows: t, S, I, D, R).

    Returns (t, X) with X of shape (m, 4) in state order (S, I, D, R).
    """
    rows = []
    with open(path, newline="") as fh:
        for rec in csv.reader(fh):
            if not rec:
                continue
            rows.append([float(v) for v in rec])
    arr = np.asarray(rows, dtype=float)
    if arr.shape[0] == 5:      # stored as [t, S, I, D, R] rows
        arr = arr.T
    t = arr[:, 0]
    X = arr[:, 1:5]
    return t, X

"""Physics-informed weak regression (PIWR) for the SIDR model.

* library A(x, t) with no unknowns, from eq. (5)                (req. R1)
* integrated weak relation x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta, eq. (12)   (req. R2)
* cubic spline (not-a-knot) interpolation of every library entry over the
  sample grid, integrated exactly from t0 to t_j, eq. (13)      (req. R3)
* x0 as n additional unknowns, augmented system, eq. (14)       (req. R4)
* column scaling to unit norm + SVD least squares (no normal
  equations), eq. (11) and the paragraph after (18)             (req. R5/R6)
* optional compartment row scaling D_n = diag(1 / max_i |x~_i,c|)
* omega = h(theta) and the delta-method covariance, eq. (19)    (req. R12)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Quadrature: weights of the exactly integrated not-a-knot cubic spline
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
def _spline_weights_cached(t_key):
    t = np.asarray(t_key, dtype=float)
    m = t.size
    # A cubic spline is linear in its data, so interpolating the columns of the
    # identity gives the m x m matrix of basis-spline integrals.
    spline = CubicSpline(t, np.eye(m), axis=0, bc_type="not-a-knot")
    anti = spline.antiderivative()
    vals = anti(t)                      # vals[j, i] = int_{t0}^{t_j} phi_i
    return vals - vals[0][None, :]      # W[j, i], W[0, :] = 0


def spline_weight_matrix(t):
    """W with J_j = sum_i W[j, i] A_i, i.e. the weights of eq. (13)."""
    t = np.ascontiguousarray(np.asarray(t, dtype=float))
    return _spline_weights_cached(t.tobytes() + str(t.size).encode()).copy()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Library of the SIDR model, eq. (5)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def library(X, N):
    """Return A with shape (m, n, p) for states x = (S, I, D, R), theta = (a,b,g).

        dS = -alpha SI/N                  -> column ( -SI/N,       0,  0)
        dI =  alpha SI/N - (beta+gamma) I -> column (  SI/N,      -I, -I)
        dD =  gamma I                     -> column (     0,       0,  I)
        dR =  beta  I                     -> column (     0,       I,  0)
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m = X.shape[0]
    S, I = X[:, 0], X[:, 1]
    inf = S * I / N
    A = np.zeros((m, 4, 3))
    A[:, 0, 0] = -inf
    A[:, 1, 0] = inf
    A[:, 1, 1] = -I
    A[:, 2, 2] = I
    A[:, 1, 2] = -I
    A[:, 3, 1] = I
    return A


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assembly and solve
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_system(X, t, N, W=None):
    """Assemble M z = y of eq. (14) with z = (theta, x0) in R^{p+n}.

    Returns M (n*m, p+n), y (n*m,), the integrated library J (m, n, p) and the
    unit-column scaling vector of M (for the covariance).
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m, n = X.shape
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    if W is None:
        W = spline_weight_matrix(t)
    A = library(X, N)
    p = A.shape[2]
    J = np.einsum("ji,irc->jrc", W, A)          # (m, n, p), J[0] == 0 exactly

    M = np.zeros((m * n, p + n))
    y = np.zeros(m * n)
    for r in range(n):                          # state equation r
        rows = np.arange(m) * n + r
        M[rows, :p] = J[:, r, :]
        M[rows, p + r] = 1.0
        y[rows] = X[:, r]
    return M, y, J


def solve_ls(M, y, column_scale=True, want_cov=True):
    """Column-scaled SVD least squares (never the normal equations)."""
    if column_scale:
        norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
        norms[norms == 0.0] = 1.0
    else:
        norms = np.ones(M.shape[1])
    Ms = M / norms[None, :]
    U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(Ms, full_matrices=False)
    rank = int(np.sum(s > (s[0] * max(Ms.shape) * np.finfo(float).eps)))
    u = Vt.T @ ((U.T @ y) / s)
    z = u / norms                                # theta = C u, C = diag(1/norms)
    info = {"rank": rank, "cond": float(s[0] / s[-1]) if s[-1] > 0 else np.inf,

        info["sigma2"] = sigma2

"""Strong-form physics-informed regression (PIR) baselines, paper section 3.1.

Used only as a cross-check of the data generation and the noise model: the
finite-difference truncation error of PIR-FD2 on noise-free SIDR data is a
deterministic property of the grid, so it can be compared with the reported
PIR-FD2 error.  The match target (C1/C2) is the PIWR estimator.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from .piwr import library, solve_ls


def fd_derivative(X, dt, order):
    """Central finite differences of order 2, 4 or 6 (paper eq. (9)).

    Returns (deriv, idx) for the interior samples where the stencil fits.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m = X.shape[0]
    if order == 2:
        h = 1
        idx = np.arange(1, m - 1)
        coefs = {-1: -0.5, 1: 0.5}
    elif order == 4:
        h = 2
        idx = np.arange(2, m - 2)
        coefs = {-2: 1.0 / 12, -1: -8.0 / 12, 1: 8.0 / 12, 2: -1.0 / 12}
    elif order == 6:
        h = 3
        idx = np.arange(3, m - 3)
        coefs = {-3: -1.0 / 60, -2: 9.0 / 60, -1: -45.0 / 60,
                 1: 45.0 / 60, 2: -9.0 / 60, 3: 1.0 / 60}
    else:  # pragma: no cover
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported finite-difference order {order}")
    deriv = np.zeros_like(X)
    for shift, c in coefs.items():
        deriv[idx] += c * X[idx + shift]
    deriv /= dt
    return deriv[idx], idx


def fit(X, t, N, order=2, row_scaling=False, column_scale=True):
    """PIR fit: A(theta) ~= b with b the finite-difference derivative."""
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    dt = float(t[1] - t[0])
    d, idx = fd_derivative(X, dt, order)
    A = library(X[idx], N)                    # (M, n, p)
    M = A.reshape(idx.size * X.shape[1], -1)
    b = d.reshape(-1)
    if row_scaling:
        s = np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)
        s[s == 0.0] = 1.0
        w = np.tile(1.0 / s, idx.size)
        M = M * w[:, None]
        b = b * w
    z, info = solve_ls(M, b, column_scale=column_scale, want_cov=False)
    return {"theta": z, "alpha": float(z[0]), "beta": float(z[1]),
            "gamma": float(z[2]), "rank": info["rank"], "cond": info["cond"],
            "M_shape": M.shape}

"""Error metrics and summaries (paper section 5.1, requirement R14)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import time

import numpy as np

from . import piwr


def pct_error(estimate, actual):
    """Percent error relative to the actual value, eq. of section 5.1."""
    return 100.0 * abs(float(estimate) - float(actual)) / abs(float(actual))


def theta_pct_errors(theta, theta_true):
    return np.array([pct_error(e, a) for e, a in zip(theta, theta_true)])


def summarize_errors(errors):
    """Summary of a set of percent errors over noise realizations."""
    e = np.asarray(errors, dtype=float)
    q = np.percentile(e, [5, 25, 50, 75, 95])
    return {
        "n": int(e.size),
        "median": float(q[2]),
        "mean": float(e.mean()),
        "std": float(e.std(ddof=1)) if e.size > 1 else 0.0,
        "q05": float(q[0]),
        "q25": float(q[1]),
        "q75": float(q[3]),
        "q95": float(q[4]),
        "min": float(e.min()),
        "max": float(e.max()),
    }


def time_fit(fit_fn, repeats=30, **kwargs):
    """Median CPU time in milliseconds of one fit (paper section 5.9)."""
    times = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        fit_fn(**kwargs)
        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3)
    times = np.asarray(times)
    return {"median_ms": float(np.median(times)), "mean_ms": float(times.mean()),
            "min_ms": float(times.min()), "max_ms": float(times.max()),
            "repeats": int(repeats)}

"""Scratch exploration (not part of the deliverable)."""
import time
import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import sidr, pir
from src.evaluate import pct_error

t = sidr.time_grid()
t0 = time.perf_counter()
X_true = sidr.simulate(t)
print("sim time", time.perf_counter() - t0)
print("X_true[0]", X_true[0], "X_true[-1]", X_true[-1])
print("max per compartment", X_true.max(axis=0))
print("I peak", X_true[:, 1].max(), "at", t[np.argmax(X_true[:, 1])])

# compare with DINN csv
tc, Xc = sidr.load_dinn_csv(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV)
print("csv shape", Xc.shape, "t range", tc[0], tc[-1])
rel = np.abs(Xc - X_true) / np.maximum(np.abs(X_true), 1e-12)
print("max rel diff vs DINN csv", rel.max(axis=0))

W = piwr.spline_weight_matrix(t)
print("W shape", W.shape, "W[0] max", np.abs(W[0]).max())

from src import piwr

# noiseless fit
for rs in (False, True):
    fit = piwr.fit(X_true, t, row_scaling=rs, W=W)
    print("rs=", rs, "alpha", fit["alpha"], "err%", pct_error(fit["alpha"], 0.191),
          "beta err%", pct_error(fit["beta"], 0.05), "gamma err%", pct_error(fit["gamma"], 0.0294),
          "x0", fit["x0"], "shape", fit["M_shape"], "rank", fit["rank"], "cond", fit["cond"])
    print("   J0", fit["J_t0_max_abs"])

# PIR baselines noise-free
for order in (2, 4, 6):
    p = pir.fit(X_true, t, C.POPULATION_N, order=order)
    errs = [pct_error(p[k], v) for k, v in zip(("alpha", "beta", "gamma"), C.THETA_TRUE)]
    print("PIR-FD", order, "alpha", p["alpha"], errs, "median", np.median(errs))

# noisy single realization
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
Xn = sidr.add_noise(X_true, 0.01, rng)
for rs in (False, True):
    fit = piwr.fit(Xn, t, row_scaling=rs, W=W)
    errs = [pct_error(fit[k], v) for k, v in zip(("alpha", "beta", "gamma"), C.THETA_TRUE)]
    print("noisy rs=", rs, "alpha err%", errs[0], "errs", errs, "median", np.median(errs))
for order in (2, 4, 6):
    p = pir.fit(Xn, t, C.POPULATION_N, order=order)
    errs = [pct_error(p[k], v) for k, v in zip(("alpha", "beta", "gamma"), C.THETA_TRUE)]
    print("noisy PIR-FD", order, errs, "median", np.median(errs))

import time
import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import sidr, pir, piwr
from src.evaluate import pct_error

t = sidr.time_grid()
X_true = sidr.simulate(t)
W = piwr.spline_weight_matrix(t)
N = C.POPULATION_N

n_draws = 200
res = {("piwr", True): [], ("piwr", False): [], ("fd2", 2): [], ("fd4", 4), ("fd6", 6): []}
res = {("piwr", True): [], ("piwr", False): [], ("fd2", 2): [], ("fd4", 4): [], ("fd6", 6): []}
t0 = time.perf_counter()
for k in range(n_draws):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + k)
    Xn = sidr.add_noise(X_true, 0.01, rng)
    for rs in (True, False):
        f = piwr.fit(Xn, t, N, row_scaling=rs, W=W, want_cov=False)
        res[("piwr", rs)].append(np.median([pct_error(f[kk], v) for kk, v in zip(("alpha", "beta", "gamma"), C.THETA_TRUE)]))

    1| """COVID-19 SIDR benchmark: generation of the synthetic data.
    2| 
    3| Paper eq. (5) / Appendix A.1:
    4|     dS/dt = -alpha S I / N
    5|     dI/dt =  alpha S I / N - (beta + gamma) I
    6|     dD/dt =  gamma I
    7|     dR/dt =  beta  I
    8| with x0 = (N-1, 1, 0, 0), (alpha, beta, gamma) = (0.191, 0.05, 0.0294),
    9| N = 59e6, and 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days.
   10| """
   11| from __future__ import annotations
   12| 
   13| import csv
   14| 
   15| import numpy as np
   16| from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
   17| 
   18| 
   19| def sidr_rhs(t, x, alpha, beta, gamma, N):
   20|     S, I, D, R = x
   21|     infection = alpha * S * I / N
   22|     return [
   23|         -infection,
   24|         infection - (beta + gamma) * I,
   25|         gamma * I,
   26|         beta * I,
   27|     ]
   28| 
   29| 
   30| def time_grid(m=100, t0=0.0, T=500.0):
   31|     """Equally spaced sample grid, endpoints included."""
   32|     return np.linspace(t0, T, m)

   34| 
   35| def simulate(t, params=(0.191, 0.05, 0.0294), x0=None, N=59e6,
   36|              rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10, method="LSODA"):
   37|     """Integrate the SIDR IVP and return the states at the sample times.
   38| 
   39|     Returns an array of shape (m, 4) with state order (S, I, D, R).
   40|     """
   41|     alpha, beta, gamma = params
   42|     if x0 is None:
   43|         x0 = (N - 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0)

   46|         sidr_rhs,
   47|         (float(t[0]), float(t[-1])),
   48|         np.asarray(x0, dtype=float),

   50|         t_eval=t,
   51|         args=(alpha, beta, gamma, N),
   52|         rtol=rtol,
   53|         atol=atol,
   54|     )

    1| """Physics-informed weak regression (PIWR) for the SIDR model.
    2| 
    3| Implements paper section 3.2:
    4| 
    5| * library A(x, t) with no unknowns, from eq. (5)                (req. R1)
    6| * integrated weak relation x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta, eq. (12)   (req. R2)
    7| * cubic spline (not-a-knot) interpolation of every library entry over the
    8|   sample grid, integrated exactly from t0 to t_j, eq. (13)      (req. R3)
    9| * x0 as n additional unknowns, augmented system, eq. (14)       (req. R4)
   10| * column scaling to unit norm + SVD least squares (no normal
   11|   equations), eq. (11) and the paragraph after (18)             (req. R5/R6)
   12| * optional compartment row scaling D_n = diag(1 / max_i |x~_i,c|)
   13| * omega = h(theta) and the delta-method covariance, eq. (19)    (req. R12)
   14| """
   15| from __future__ import annotations
   16| 
   17| from functools import lru_cache
   18| 
   19| import numpy as np
   20| from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
   21| 
   22| 
   23| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   24| # Quadrature: weights of the exactly integrated not-a-knot cubic spline
   25| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   26| @lru_cache(maxsize=32)
   27| def _spline_weights_cached(t_key):
   28|     t = np.frombuffer(t_key, dtype=float).copy()
   29|     m = t.size
   30|     # A cubic spline is linear in its data, so interpolating the columns of the
   31|     # identity gives the m x m matrix of basis-spline integrals.
   32|     spline = CubicSpline(t, np.eye(m), axis=0, bc_type="not-a-knot")
   33|     anti = spline.antiderivative()
   34|     vals = anti(t)                      # vals[j, i] = int_{t0}^{t_j} phi_i
   35|     return vals - vals[0][None, :]      # W[j, i], W[0, :] = 0
   36| 
   37| 
   38| def spline_weight_matrix(t):
   39|     """W with J_j = sum_i W[j, i] A_i, i.e. the weights of eq. (13)."""
   40|     t = np.ascontiguousarray(np.asarray(t, dtype=float))
   41|     return _spline_weights_cached(t.tobytes()).copy()
   42| 
   43| 
   44| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   45| # Library of the SIDR model, eq. (5)
   46| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   47| def library(X, N):
   48|     """Return A with shape (m, n, p) for states x = (S, I, D, R), theta = (a,b,g).

   51|         dI =  alpha SI/N - (beta+gamma) I -> column (  SI/N,      -I, -I)

   57|     S, I = X[:, 0], X[:, 1]
   58|     inf = S * I / N
   59|     A = np.zeros((m, 4, 3))

"""Reproduce the COVID-19 SIDR PIWR parameter-estimation results (claims C1, C2).

Usage
-----
    python reproduce.py            # full run, writes results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # fast consistency checks only

The script re-implements the paper's PIWR estimator (physics-informed weak
regression, section 3.2) from the equations: the SIDR library is interpolated
with a not-a-knot cubic spline, the spline is integrated exactly to every
sample time, the initial state is estimated jointly, the augmented system is
column-scaled and solved by an SVD least-squares solve.  Nothing here uses the
authors' code (they released only the DINN baseline notebooks).

Every reported number is computed here from the simulated benchmark.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

import config as C

from src.evaluate import pct_error, summarize_errors, theta_pct_errors


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Benchmark data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_benchmark():
    """Simulate the SIDR benchmark and cross-check it against the DINN CSV."""
    t = sidr.time_grid(C.M_SAMPLES, C.T_START, C.T_END)
    X_true = sidr.simulate(t, C.THETA_TRUE, C.X0_TRUE, C.POPULATION_N,
                           rtol=C.ODE_RTOL, atol=C.ODE_ATOL, method=C.ODE_METHOD)
    info = {"source": "regenerated from Appendix A.1 with LSODA (rtol=atol=1e-10)"}
    if os.path.exists(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV):

        rel = np.abs(X_csv - X_true) / np.maximum(np.abs(X_true), 1e-300)
        info.update({
            "dinn_csv": os.path.relpath(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV),
            "dinn_csv_shape": list(X_csv.shape),
            "dinn_csv_t_range": [float(t_csv[0]), float(t_csv[-1])],
            "max_rel_diff_vs_lsoda": float(rel.max()),
            "dinn_csv_is_noisefree": bool(np.allclose(X_csv, X_true, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-3)),

        "D_R_non_decreasing": bool(np.all(np.diff(X_true[:, 2]) >= 0)

def build_benchmark():
    """Simulate the SIDR benchmark and check every shipped DINN SIDR CSV.

    The DINN repository ships only noise-free SIDR tables, so the 1 % noise of
    claim C1 is added here (requirement R7) rather than read from a file.
    """
    t = sidr.time_grid(C.M_SAMPLES, C.T_START, C.T_END)
    X_true = sidr.simulate(t, C.THETA_TRUE, C.X0_TRUE, C.POPULATION_N,
                           rtol=C.ODE_RTOL, atol=C.ODE_ATOL, method=C.ODE_METHOD)
    info = {
        "source": ("regenerated from Appendix A.1 with LSODA (rtol=atol=1e-10) "
                   "and 1 % noise added per R7"),
        "candidate_csvs": {},
    }
    candidates = [
        C.DINN_SIDR_CSV,
        os.path.join(C.REPO, "Experiments", "noise", "sidr_100_pts.csv"),
        os.path.join(C.REPO, "Experiments", "param_ranges", "sidr_100_pts.csv"),
        os.path.join(C.REPO, "Experiments", "different_architectures", "covid_100_pts.csv"),
    ]
    any_noisy = False
    for path in candidates:
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            continue
        t_csv, X_csv = sidr.load_dinn_csv(path)
        rel = np.abs(X_csv - X_true) / np.maximum(np.abs(X_true), 1e-300)
        noisy = bool(rel.max() > 1e-3)
        any_noisy = any_noisy or noisy
        info["candidate_csvs"][os.path.relpath(path).replace("\\", "/")] = {
            "shape": list(X_csv.shape),
            "t_range": [float(t_csv[0]), float(t_csv[-1])],
            "max_rel_diff_vs_lsoda": float(rel.max()),
            "contains_measurement_noise": noisy,
        }
    if C.DINN_SIDR_CSV in candidates and os.path.exists(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV):
        info["primary_csv"] = os.path.relpath(C.DINN_SIDR_CSV).replace("\\", "/")
        info["primary_csv_max_rel_diff_vs_lsoda"] = info["candidate_csvs"][
            info["primary_csv"]]["max_rel_diff_vs_lsoda"]
        info["shipped_noisy_sidr_csv_found"] = bool(any_noisy)
        info["primary_csv_is_noisefree"] = not any_noisy
    info["noise_added_here"] = True
    return t, X_true, info


def noise_model_check(X_true, eps, n_draws=200):
    """Empirical verification of requirement R7 / Appendix A.18.

    For each compartment the realized residual standard deviation must equal
    eps * max_t |x_c(t)| of the *true* trajectory.
    """
    out = {"n_draws": int(n_draws), "eps": float(eps)}
    for j, name in enumerate(C.STATE_ORDER):
        resid = []
        for k in range(n_draws):
            rng = np.random.default_rng(90_000 + k)
            Xn = sidr.add_noise(X_true, eps, rng)
            resid.append(Xn[:, j] - X_true[:, j])
        resid = np.concatenate(resid)
        expected = eps * float(np.abs(X_true[:, j]).max())
        out[name] = {
            "empirical_sd": float(resid.std(ddof=1)),
            "empirical_mean": float(resid.mean()),
            "expected_sd": float(expected),
            "relative_sd_error": float(abs(resid.std(ddof=1) - expected) / expected),
            "max_abs_residual": float(np.abs(resid).max()),
        }
    out["max_relative_sd_error"] = max(v["relative_sd_error"] for k, v in out.items()
                                       if isinstance(v, dict))
    return out

def row_scaling_tuning(t, X_true, W, eps, n_draws=None, seed_offset=10_000):
    """Tune the row-scaling choice on draws that are NOT the reported ones.

    Paper section 5.1: "the row scaling ... is decided per model and estimator on
    100 draws".  Column scaling is applied after the row scaling in all cases.
    The reported realizations use seeds [SEED_BASE, SEED_BASE+N); the tuning
    block starts at `seed_offset` so the two never overlap.
    """
    n_draws = C.N_TUNING_DRAWS if n_draws is None else n_draws
    per = {False: {"alpha": [], "med": [], "sigma": []},
           True: {"alpha": [], "med": [], "sigma": []}}
    for k in range(n_draws):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed_offset + k)
        Xn = sidr.add_noise(X_true, eps, rng)
        for rs in (False, True):
            f = piwr.fit(Xn, t, C.POPULATION_N, row_scaling=rs, W=W, want_cov=True)
            e = theta_pct_errors(f["theta"], C.THETA_TRUE)
            per[rs]["alpha"].append(float(e[0]))
            per[rs]["med"].append(float(np.median(e)))
            per[rs]["sigma"].append(100.0 * float(f["sigma_theta"][0])
                                    / C.TRUE_PARAMS["alpha"])
    out = {"n_tuning_draws": int(n_draws), "seed_block": [seed_offset, seed_offset + n_draws - 1],
           "noise_eps": float(eps), "variants": {}}
    for rs in (False, True):
        a = np.asarray(per[rs]["alpha"])
        m = np.asarray(per[rs]["med"])
        s = np.asarray(per[rs]["sigma"])
        out["variants"]["row_scaling_%s" % rs] = {
            "alpha_pct_error": summarize_errors(a),
            "median_over_parameters": summarize_errors(m),
            "median_alpha_error_over_ls_sigma": float(np.median(a / s)),
            "empirical_sd_over_median_ls_sigma": float(a.std(ddof=1) / np.median(s)),
            "median_ls_sigma_pct": float(np.median(s)),
        }
    d = np.asarray(per[True]["alpha"]) - np.asarray(per[False]["alpha"])
    out["paired_alpha_difference_on"] = summarize_errors(d)
    out["paired_mean_difference"] = float(d.mean())
    out["paired_se_of_mean"] = float(d.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(d.size))
    out["paired_fraction_on_better"] = float(np.mean(np.abs(per[True]["alpha"])
                                                     < np.abs(per[False]["alpha"])))
    return out

"""Scratch: compare the two noise conventions (not deliverable)."""
import numpy as np

import config as C
from src import sidr, piwr
from src.evaluate import pct_error, theta_pct_errors

t = sidr.time_grid()
X_true = sidr.simulate(t)
W = piwr.spline_weight_matrix(t)
names = ("alpha", "beta", "gamma")


def mult_noise(X, eps, rng):
    """DINN notebook recipe: x~ = (1 + eps*xi) * x, per sample, per compartment."""
    xi = rng.standard_normal(X.shape)
    return X * (1.0 + eps * xi)


for eps in (0.0, 0.01):
    for conv, gen in (("additive_max", lambda X, r: sidr.add_noise(X, eps, r)),
                      ("multiplicative", lambda X, r: mult_noise(X, eps, r))):
        if eps == 0.0 and conv == "multiplicative":
            continue
        out = []
        for k in range(50):
            rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + k)
            Xn = gen(X_true, rng)
            f = piwr.fit(Xn, t, C.POPULATION_N, row_scaling=True, W=W, want_cov=False)
            out.append(theta_pct_errors(f["theta"], C.THETA_TRUE))
        out = np.asarray(out)
        print("eps=%g %-16s" % (eps, conv),
              " ".join("%s med %.4f" % (n, np.median(out[:, j])) for j, n in enumerate(names)),
              "| median-over-params %.4f" % np.median(np.median(out, axis=1)),
              "| alpha q05 %.3f q95 %.3f" % (np.percentile(out[:, 0], 5), np.percentile(out[:, 0], 95)))

# single seed-0 realizations, both conventions
for conv, gen in (("additive_max", lambda X, r: sidr.add_noise(X, 0.01, r)),

n = 100


def sweep(gen, eps):
    res = {k: [] for k in ("FD2", "FD4", "FD6", "PIWR")}

        Xn = gen(X_true, eps, rng)

    return {k: float(np.median(v)) for k, v in res.items()}


for label, gen in (("additive_max", lambda X, e, r: sidr.add_noise(X, e, r)),

def build_system(X, t, N, W=None, joint_x0=True):
    """Assemble M z = y of eq. (14) with z = (theta, x0) in R^{p+n}.

    With ``joint_x0=False`` the identity block is dropped and the system is
    solved for theta only (used only for the fixed-x0 diagnostic).

    Returns M (n*m, p+n) [or (n*m, p)], y (n*m,), the integrated library
    J (m, n, p), whose first row vanishes exactly.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m, n = X.shape
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    if W is None:
        W = spline_weight_matrix(t)
    A = library(X, N)
    p = A.shape[2]
    J = np.einsum("ji,irc->jrc", W, A)          # (m, n, p), J[0] == 0 exactly

    M = np.zeros((m * n, p + n if joint_x0 else p))
    y = np.zeros(m * n)
    for r in range(n):                          # state equation r
        rows = np.arange(m) * n + r
        M[rows, :p] = J[:, r, :]
        if joint_x0:
            M[rows, p + r] = 1.0
        y[rows] = X[:, r]
    return M, y, J

def build_system(X, t, N, W=None):
    """Assemble M z = y of eq. (14) with z = (theta, x0) in R^{p+n}.

    Returns M (n*m, p+n), y (n*m,), the integrated library J (m, n, p) and the
    unit-column scaling vector of M (for the covariance).
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    m, n = X.shape
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=float)
    if W is None:
        W = spline_weight_matrix(t)
    A = library(X, N)
    p = A.shape[2]
    J = np.einsum("ji,irc->jrc", W, A)          # (m, n, p), J[0] == 0 exactly

    M = np.zeros((m * n, p + n))
    y = np.zeros(m * n)
    for r in range(n):                          # state equation r
        rows = np.arange(m) * n + r
        M[rows, :p] = J[:, r, :]
        M[rows, p + r] = 1.0
        y[rows] = X[:, r]
    return M, y, J

def diagnostics_table(t, X_true, W, use_row_scaling, n_draws=None, seed_offset=20_000):
    """Error-vs-LS-sigma diagnostics on a fixed, pre-declared draw block.

    Variants (all with the paper's additive R7 noise unless stated):
      joint_x0          : paper's estimator, library evaluated at noisy states
      joint_x0_cleanlib : library built from noiseless states (errors-in-
                          variables diagnostic for the alpha column)
      fixed_x0          : x0 pinned at the truth (diagnostic only)
      notebook_relative : the DINN notebook's multiplicative noise, verbatim
    For every variant both the alpha % error and the median-over-parameters
    % error are reported, plus the median LS sigma and their ratio.
    """
    n_draws = C.N_DIAGNOSTIC_DRAWS if n_draws is None else n_draws
    variants = {}

    def run(name, gen, **kw):
        a, med, sig, bs, gs = [], [], [], [], []
        for k in range(n_draws):
            rng = np.random.default_rng(seed_offset + k)
            Xn = gen(X_true, rng)
            f = piwr.fit(Xn, t, C.POPULATION_N, row_scaling=use_row_scaling,
                         W=W, want_cov=True, **kw)
            e = theta_pct_errors(f["theta"], C.THETA_TRUE)
            a.append(float(e[0]))
            bs.append(float(e[1]))
            gs.append(float(e[2]))
            med.append(float(np.median(e)))
            sig.append(100.0 * float(f["sigma_theta"][0]))
        a, med, sig = np.asarray(a), np.asarray(med), np.asarray(sig)
        variants[name] = {
            "alpha_pct_error": summarize_errors(a),
            "beta_pct_error_median": float(np.median(bs)),
            "gamma_pct_error_median": float(np.median(gs)),
            "median_over_parameters_pct_error": summarize_errors(med),
            "median_ls_sigma_alpha_pct": float(np.median(sig)),
            "median_alpha_error_over_ls_sigma": float(np.median(a / sig)),
        }

    add = lambda X, r: sidr.add_noise(X, C.NOISE_EPS_SMALL, r)
    rel = lambda X, r: sidr.add_relative_noise(X, C.NOISE_EPS_SMALL, r)
    run("joint_x0", add)
    run("joint_x0_clean_library", add, x_lib=X_true)
    run("fixed_x0_at_truth", add, x0_fixed=np.asarray(C.X0_TRUE))
    run("notebook_relative_noise", rel)
    run("notebook_relative_noise_clean_library", rel, x_lib=X_true)
    return {"n_draws": int(n_draws), "seed_block": [seed_offset, seed_offset + n_draws - 1],
            "row_scaling": bool(use_row_scaling), "variants": variants}

args.rationale: The DINN repo ships only the noise-free SIDR table (verified: max rel. diff 2.2e-7 vs my LSODA trajectory), so no shipped noisy realization exists to fit. The estimator is unbiased (mean signed alpha error ~0), so no seed can be chosen to hit 0.124 % legitimately; the distribution is the honest, reproducible quantity. Note that the paper's reported 0.124 % lies at the ~11th percentile of the 1000-draw distribution (7 % of draws below 0.1 %, 17 % below 0.25 %), i.e. it is a favourable but entirely possible draw. target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

audit_summary: The code implements the target PIWR estimator faithfully for the SIDR benchmark: parameter-linear library, not-a-knot cubic-spline quadrature, joint initial-state estimation, column scaling, SVD least squares, LSODA tolerances, and the paper's additive max-scaled noise recipe. The noise-free fit matches C2 essentially exactly (0.000105489% versus 0.000105%), and the PIR-FD2 baseline is close to the paper's reported scale, validating the data generation and solve. The clean rerun's headline value is, however, 0.7175% median alpha error over 1000 noise draws, well outside the 0.1116-0.1364% tolerance around C1's 0.124%; the single pre-declared seed-0 draw is 0.9828%, and only 1.7% of the 1000 draws land inside the band. The paper's 0.124% is an unseeded single realization and lies near the 11th percentile of this distribution, so the mismatch is dominated by noise-draw randomness and paper underspecification, not an obvious estimator bug. The conformal requirements R8-R11 are not implemented, which does not affect the C1 point estimate but means the workspace is not a full paper reproduction; the paper constants in config.py are reference-only and are not used to compute the reported fit value.

requirement_check.evidence: src/piwr.py library() builds A with columns -SI/N, SI/N, -I, I for theta=(alpha,beta,gamma); no unknown parameters enter the library.
build_system() uses J = W @ A and y = X, forming x(tj)=x0+J_j theta without differentiating the data; J[0] is zero.
spline_weight_matrix() uses scipy.interpolate.CubicSpline with bc_type='not-a-knot' on the identity and integrates its antiderivative exactly.
build_system() appends an identity block for x0; fit() defaults to joint_x0=True and reports the estimated x0.
solve_ls() uses numpy.linalg.svd and does not form normal equations; rank and condition number are logged.
solve_ls() scales columns to unit norm before the SVD and rescales the solution afterwards.
sidr.add_noise() uses residual sd eps*max_t|x_c(t)| per compartment; the empirical noise check reports max relative sd error 0.0084.
No conformal calibration prior-box code is implemented; the workspace only performs point-estimate PIWR fits.
No split-conformal maximum-normalized-error score or simultaneous quantile is implemented.
No PIWR-RACC residual-adaptive h=1+R/Rbar layer is implemented.
No 999-calibration-problem / alpha=0.1 conformal run is present.
piwr.h() is the identity for SIDR, and delta_method_sigma() plus the SVD covariance give sigma_theta/sigma_x0.
config.py sets N=59e6, x0=(N-1,1,0,0), alpha=0.191, beta=0.05, gamma=0.0294, and 100 linspace samples on [0,500] days.
evaluate.pct_error() computes 100*|estimate-actual|/|actual|; theta_pct_errors() and median-over-parameters summaries are implemented.
sidr.simulate() calls solve_ivp with method='LSODA', rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10.
